dataset.description: Sample collection and processing complies with EU animal welfare regulations. Animal manipulation complies with the guidelines of the European Union Directive (2010/63/EU) and the Italian Legislative Decree 26 of March 4, 2014. The general objective of the project is to assess how the ingestion of MPs through the diet may affect the health status of gilthead seabream, a commercially important species of high economic value and among the most demanded, both wild-caught and farmed. The aim is therefore to analyze how MPs, once adsorbed with environmental pollutants, can interfere at both metabolic and reproductive levels and may also affect fillet quality, as well as how the co-administration of a postbiotic could mitigate their potential toxicity. Thus considery the complexity, the work couldn't be carried out without conducting experiments or other scientific procedures on living animals.

This data management plan will outline the results of study PID 37349 - PFAS, Microplastics, and Seabream Health: Assessing Risks and the Protective Role of Postbiotics.
The datasets to be generated from the project are

- omic data  from gonads, liver, brain, muscle
- qPCR validation data

dmp.description: The project investigates the biological effects of dietary exposure to microplastics (MPs) and PFAS-adsorbed MPs in seabream, focusing on metabolism and reproductive health. It also explores the potential of dietary post-biotics as a mitigation strategy against the toxicity of these environmental contaminants. Experimental data will support early-warning systems and inform regulatory bodies and stakeholders to improve plastic and PFAS management, promoting sustainable and health-protective interventions.This DMP describes the management of biological, genomic and phenotypic data generated in the  project.  It will ensures compliance with FAIR principles, ethical standards, and AquaServ open data policies.
